title.narrative: Coastal Oasis: Bridging Biodiversity, Livelihoods, Equity and Equality in the Yawri Bay of Sierra Leone

description.narrative: Impact: Local communities contribute to the protection of the ecosystems of the Yawri Bay MPA.Outcome:2880 project participants implement localized MPA management plans and sustainable income practices that protect the ecosystems in the Yawri Bay MPA.

Problem statement: Biodiversity loss threatens coastal ecosystems and livelihoods of communities dependent on them, exacerbating existing inequality and poverty. Target group and intervention area: 2.880 women, youths and other marginalized groups in Yawri Bay. Overall objective: Foster resilient coastal communities by integrating biodiversity conservation, sustainable livelihoods and equality of women and men. Outputs: strengthened MPA management structures, strengthened awareness and participation in MPA management, sustainable income-generating activities that promote equity and inclusivity; partner capacity development on finance and MEAL.1 Partner: CSSL (partner since 5 years)

The proposed project targets eight communities in three chiefdoms: Ribbi (33,165 inhabitants), Bumpeh (37,445 inhabitants), and Kargboro (34,862 inhabitants according to the 2015 census): Fogbo (estimated population: 2,700, community estimate), Youndu (approx. 1,500), Katta, Plantain Island (approx. 3,000), Kent (approx. 2,000), Suen, Bondatok (approx. 800), Moyeamoh (approx. 500), and Tombo (approx. 20,000). There will be no overlap with participants in other BMZ-funded or similar projects, as this is a criterion for exclusion from participation. However, synergies and the exchange of learning experiences with a possible Well-Found project will be examined and utilized. CSSL selected these communities based on their significant negative impact on the MPA and its biodiversity, taking into account the degree of degradation, willingness to participate in project implementation, commitment, and vulnerability to climate shocks.The project will target 2,880 direct project participants (50% women, 50% youth). Through the overall activities of the project, in particular through community action plans and local statutes to protect valuable ecosystems that benefit the entire community, as well as through income-generating measures and the resulting higher incomes that benefit the entire families of the participants (average household size in Sierra Leone: 6 people), and through broad-based awareness-raising measures, are expected to indirectly reach around 30,000 people, the entire population of the target communities (according to estimates). They will benefit from improved environmental awareness thanks to large-scale communication campaigns, as well as healthier ecosystems and restored natural resources thanks to better management of the marine protected area and reforestation initiatives in their communities.
